amendments.alias_rule: data/scripts/x5_density.py build_lga_aliases: for each HFR facility, the nearest GRID3 facility within 2 km in the same state, never the one sharing its source id, votes for its LGA name; an HFR LGA name with at least 10 votes, 60% or more for one differently written GRID3 name, is an alias of it. No id and no label is used
amendments.change: in both arms, 'LGA agree' compares the GRID3 LGA name with the HFR LGA name read through an alias table, instead of exact folded equality. The reviewer noticed that FCT's 'Abuja Municipal Area Council' (GRID3) and 'Municipal Area Council' (HFR) counted as different LGAs: 185 of FCT's 512 twins sharing a source id, 36%. Nationally, exact equality calls 3,942 of 42,010 twins different LGAs
amendments.rejected_alternative: fuzzy name similarity (edit ratio >= 0.8 or token subset) would also have fixed spellings, but called 58 pairs of distinct LGAs in one state the same (Abeokuta North / South, Ibadan North / North East)
amendments.unchanged: rule (rule_sha256 still matches), arms otherwise, development labels, cross-encoder weights, test pack and kinds

expectation: density helps in the dense part of FCT (Abuja municipal) and changes little elsewhere; FCT is less dense than Lagos, so a pass here is weaker evidence for Lagos-like cities
facility_level: not used: X3 found no measurable gain, and facilities are upgraded, so the registries' levels need not agree for one facility
known_risks: shared source ids are shown to the reviewer
FCT has 111 held pairs, so the review band verdict rests on about 110 pairs
the density count includes HFR duplicates of the facility itself, which inflates n slightly
question: With local facility density as a feature, does the pair decider keep errors and false merges in bound in a held-out city (FCT)?

arms.control: [cross-encoder logit, log1p km, LGA agree, coordinates missing]
arms.density: control plus log(n * (d / 2 km)^2 + 0.05) and log1p(n), where n = other HFR facilities within 2 km of the GRID3 point (HFR national coordinates, the pair's HFR record excluded) and d = km between the two points; both 0 when a point is missing
arms.reference: match-everything, scored under the same rule; it must fail

rule.cross_encoder: X0's recipe with Edo, Kano, Ondo, Lagos and FCT held out; weights pinned below
rule.density_helps: the density arm passes, and on every seed it auto-matches no more different pairs than control
rule.development: 1,110 labelled pairs: corrected 2026-08-19 and X1 copies, near-miss, X3 and X4 packs, with the X4 corrections file (2 pairs to can't tell, from the reviewer's stated intent)
rule.error_bound: errors among auto-decided <= 3% and Wilson 95% upper bound <= 10%
rule.false_merge_bound: different pairs auto-matched / all different pairs <= 2% and Wilson 95% upper bound <= 5%
rule.informative: void unless the test holds at least 60 different pairs
rule.pass: informative, and every seed meets fewer_held, error_bound and false_merge_bound on the whole pack
rule.population: the X5 pack (data/review_packs/nigeria_facilities_fct_x5_2026-11-22, 200 FCT pairs: 110 review_band, 45 lookalike, 45 near_miss) marked same_entity or different; read once, after this file
rule.review_band: reported on its own: every seed of the density arm meets fewer_held and error_bound on the review_band pairs

test.blind: the reviewer sees neither the engine's decision nor the pair's kind
test.construction: data/scripts/build_x5_pack.py (build_x4_pack.py with STATE = 'Fct'): 110 of the engine's 111 FCT review pairs (one per GRID3 facility), 45 lookalike and 45 near_miss; every row 'review', no score, kind kept out of the pack

why: X4 failed in Lagos: dense-city pairs with near-identical names, same LGA, 0-500 m apart, were auto-matched; distance and LGA agreement meant one facility in Edo, Kano and Ondo but not in Lagos. Median other HFR facilities within 2 km of a development pair: Lagos 42, Edo 5, Ondo 3, Kano 2
